steps.text: Brown beef in a large skillet over medium heat until no longer pink; drain. Add cream cheese, salt, and chili powder; mix and simmer for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add pasta and cook until al dente, 8 to 10 minutes; drain. Toss cooked shells in butter.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Fill shells with beef mixture and arrange in a 9x13-inch baking dish; pour taco sauce over shells. Cover with foil and bake in preheated oven for 15 minutes.
Remove the dish from the oven and top with Cheddar cheese, Monterey Jack cheese, and then tortilla chips. Return the dish to the oven to cook for 15 minutes more.
Top with sour cream and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Tacos in Pasta Shells
raw_recipe.description: These tacos in pasta shells are easy and fun to make. Jumbo shells get stuffed with beef, cheese, and chili seasoning, and more before getting baked.

video.description: Please the adults and the kids at dinnertime with this easy family-friendly recipe full of Mexican flavors that everyone craves. Cook up ground beef, then simmer with cream cheese, salt and chili powder. Cook large pasta shells and mix with butter. Fill up the pasta shells with the beef mixture, cover with taco sauce and bake, then top with Cheddar and Monterey Jack cheeses and crispy tortilla chips and bake some more. Serve with sour cream, green onions, tomatoes, lettuce, black olives and hot sauce!

review.reviewBody: A wonderfully creative twist and addition to basic Mexican cuisine! This is one creative cook to think of using large pasta shells in a Mexican dish! My hat go off to you, Grannycancook! I did follow the advise that quite a few had in using taco seasoning in place of the chili powder and salt. I used an envelope to 1 lb ground turkey. Also added 1/2 tsp minced garlic and 1 can diced tomatoes with green chilis (Rotel brand). Instead of taco sauce I substituted red enchilada sauce (28 oz) pouring a thin layer on the bottom of the baking dish before filling with a layer of the stuffed pasta shells and pouring rest of sauce to cover the shells. Once they were baked I topped with chopped fresh cilantro, sliced black olives, sliced green onions and fresh diced tomatoes. For sides I served refried beans covered with enchilada sauce and melted Mexican blend cheese and Lime Cilantro Rice following recipe from this web site. Excellent, excellent meal!

I like this recipe. Make a few extra shells in case some boil apart. The good thing is if you don't, you can just overfill the remaining shells. There's just 2 of us so having a full 18 wasn't an issue. I added a little extra chili powder and about a 1/2 tsp garlic powder. Also cooked the meat with onions and canned green chili's (medium). Lastly, I didn't have any regular monterey jack cheese so I grated pepper jack and used with a 3 cheese cheese cheddar mix (sharp, medium, white). I put a little sauce on the bottom of the pan to help to stop sticking as others mentioned and it worked well. I didnt use tortilla chips this time either. My bf thought it was a little salty, but also salted prior to tasting. I didn't add extra salt and I didn't think it was too salty. I found it rather yummy! I've made it before, just like the recipe states, and I found the little tweaks made it better.

These are so pretty and rather tasty as well. ..but I made quite a few changes. I only used 1 pound of ground beef because that is how I package my meat... and I can't seem to brown ground beef without onion (ever). I used 4 ounces of cream cheese and an envelope of taco seasoning in lieu of the salt and chili powder. I added a can of Ro-tel (drained) to the meat mixture and let the meat mixture sit for about an hour before stuffing the shells. I put about a cup of bottled salsa down in the pan before adding the stuffed shells and used almost all of a 10 ounce can of enchilada sauce for the top. I cooked covered for 30 minutes and uncovered for 15. This is really odd but I did not use all of the cheese...maybe 1 1/2 cups worth and only about a cup of the tortilla chips which I almost left out based on other reviews but I'm glad I didn't. I prettied it up with some chopped cilantro after cooking. Very pretty presentation served with Chef John's Spicy Spanish-Style Rice.

This was great! Mexican food and all pasta are my daughter's two favorite things, so I knew this would be a winner for sure! My changes were as follows: I used ground turkey, added black beans and corn, made my own "taco sauce" with tomato sauce thinned out with water and seasoned with cumin, chili powder, garlic and onion powders, salt and pepper, I omitted the butter, using EVOO instead and I did not use the tortilla chips as I forgot about them, but can see how the crunch would be good! We topped with sour cream and they were a hit! Thanks for this recipe!

Really liked this one. Great base recipe but made a few changes. I used a packet of taco seasoning mix (followed directions on back) and small onion with the meat when browning for more flavor. I used sour cream and chive cream cheese instead of plain. Instead of a cup of sauce I used 1 - 16 oz salsa jar. I poured some in with meat once browned, poured a small amount on bottom of baking dish so they don't stick leaving the rest for the topping. I had a little trouble with my chips getting a little to brown so I would put them on with about 10 minutes left. In the end I topped with sour cream, black olives, green onion, fresh tomato and a little cilantro once shells were out of oven. Delicious. Great leftovers also.

I had medium shells on hand so made more of a taco casserole. I added onion powder for some additional flavor and salsa instead of taco seasoning. This is a great base recipe that allows for substitutions based on what's in the pantry and fridge.

These were phenomenal. I used shredded chicken as the meat, and used 3 ounces of onion and chive cream cheese spread instead of regular cream cheese. The result was creamy and flavorful. We WILL be making these again. (Edit: This recipe hasn't QUITE replaced tacos in our house, but has come close. These are delicious and easily customized to each individual's taste. Very creative, as well.)

I have made this a few times and it is always nice. I soften onion with the meat (or veggie meat) with jalapeno then and add garlic....I use a good amount of taco seasoning, cumin and chili powder. Add a bit of broth(chicken or veg) and simmer for thirty minutes or so before adding the (limited) cheese...cottage and whatever I have seems to do well...never used cream cheese out of preference. I add a variety of toppings to the stuffed shells...cilantro, onion, olives, avocado, sour cream, queso or pico,...whatever you like! Thankyou!

Very tasty. Used picante sauce instead of taco sauce and poured some at bottom of the dish before placing shells in as others suggested. Also used both taco seasoning and chili powder for more flavor.

I made it and the family loved it. I used extra ground beef and doubled the cream cheese in it. I did not add any butter and for spices I used a package of taco seasoning. I sautéed onions and garlic and added to the ground beef and cream cheese mix then I stuffed the shells. I laid a single layer of the stuffed shells on a cookie sheet and froze them then sealed them. Then when it was the day I needed them I just took frozen shells out put them in a single layer in a casserole dish on top of a jar of tomato sauce and bake them Just before serving I talked with a layer of Mexican grated cheese mix and let them out and serve them immediately. On the table I had bowls of the usual taco toppings shredded lettuce green onions cheddar salsa baked beans chopped tomatoes and sour cream. This way everyone was able to dress Bears as they like them and then I had nacho chips on the table to crush and top it all if you chose to

I modified this recipe and will definitely make it again. I used a 375 g package of elbow macaroni instead of stuffing pasta shells and I used a 430 ml jar of medium salsa instead of taco sauce. I would use less pasta next time, maybe 280 g and I would use more salsa; up to twice as much). I doubled the chili powder and added 1/2 tsp of cayenne pepper. I used onion and chive cream cheese instead of plain. Instead of adding the crushed tortilla chips and baking in the oven, I served them as a condiment. It's a quick and easy dish to prepare and suitable for a family meal or casual company dinner. The toppings served separately make it a little more fun.

I have been making this for many years. I do use a low sodium pre made taco seasoning packet, and more taco sauce than the recipe calls for as we are a "saucy" family. It's a great change of pace from tacos. Finding the jumbo pasta shells is much more difficult these days tho.

These were very filling and we only ate two each. Knowing that we like spice, I measured heavy on the chili powder as there wasn't anything else besides salt to carry the flavor. The filling was really rich and the cheese was heavy. I cut this in half and made 10 pasta shells. I did have to allow some cooling time before I could handle the pasta. I didn't cook the pasta thoroughly but it still tore apart when handling even though I was very gentle with the shells. No matter, it will still taste the same. I didn't "simmer" the cream cheese and meat as it made a paste and there wasn't any liquid to simmer in. The filling was easy to stuff as the cream cheese held the loose meat together well especially once it cooled enough to handle easily. There didn't seem to be enough taco sauce though, and I drizzled it on as evenly as I could. This was really dry going into the oven so I was concerned that the shells would dry out and get hard. It didn't. This turned out fine. While this was okay, it wasn't good enough to fix again. There was nothing particularly wrong with it. We'd rather have had enchiladas for the work involved. I think we just like the corn tortilla base over the wheat based pasta, and enchilada sauce feels like it would have been a better choice over the taco sauce. There was no way to plate this up where it looked pretty. It came out how it came out.

This is what I make every year on my birthday (my husband tries…but in the end, I take over, haha). This is absolute favorite recipe I’ve found on All Recipes. I love a lot of others but this by far my favorite.
I have been making this for years. My grown children still request it. So good! I always double it.
I used all vegan ingredients. I veganized it all.
Delicious and easy to make. The photo does show sliced black olives, yet there is no mention of them in the recipe. Assuming it is an extra garnish rather than being baked with the shells??
